title: Exact Gilbert--Varshamov distance for rate-one-half quantum LDPC codes
source: Mittal, Srivastava, Tulsiani and Wootters ask in Section~1 whether quantum LDPC codes can reach the quantum Gilbert--Varshamov bound. Equation~\eqref{eq:gvq-rate-distance} specializes their question to binary codes and rate $1/2$ with one fixed bound on generator weight and incidence \sourcecite{ref:gvq-mstw}{MSTW26}.
progress: Mittal, Srivastava, Tulsiani and Wootters show that for each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, sparse qubit stabilizer codes of rate $1/2$ can have normalized distance at least $\delta_*-\varepsilon$. The required check-weight bound depends on $\varepsilon$, so choosing successively smaller $\varepsilon$ gives no single bound for the endpoint \sourcecite{ref:gvq-mstw}{MSTW26}.

Kasai's Corollary~5.2 attains the CSS Gilbert--Varshamov benchmark for a collection of finite-degree ensembles. Section~2.4 explains that sparsity of the extended system does not establish bounded-weight measurements of the compressed physical syndromes \sourcecite{ref:gvq-kasai}{Kas26}.

comment: The locality constant must stay fixed as $n$ grows, including at exact asymptotic equality. The related \href{https://qiqc-op.com/problem/op_4830398d0c2feb5f/}{Pauli hashing-bound question} uses stochastic errors. The \href{https://qiqc-op.com/problem/op_edcb345719181830/}{qubit distance-bound question} asks for tightness of an upper bound across rates. The catalog and literature were checked through November 26, 2026.
